sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite — Gemini API
sources.evidence: Identifies stable gemini-3.1-flash-lite. Lists 1,048,576 input tokens, 65,536 output tokens, text/image/video/audio/PDF input, text output, thinking and function calling. Describes low latency and high-volume workflows.

sources.title: Gemini API release notes — May 7 and March 3, 2026
sources.evidence: May 7 explicitly releases gemini-3.1-flash-lite as GA. March 3 launches Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Preview; May 25 shuts down gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview in favor of the stable model.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite — Google Cloud model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact model ID is gemini-3.1-flash-lite, with GA release May 7, 2026. Independently lists 1,048,576 context, 65,536 maximum output, thinking, function calling and multimodal input.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Model Card — updated May 2026
sources.evidence: The exact-model card links Gemini 3 Pro for its architecture. Describes Gemini 3 family membership and API distribution under service terms. It supplies no total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Pro Model Card — updated May 2026
sources.evidence: The architecture source expressly referenced by the Flash-Lite card describes a sparse mixture-of-experts Transformer, with routing to a subset of parameters per token. Names Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite among dependent models, without its parameter counts.

sources.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite Model Card — July 21, 2026
sources.evidence: Later sibling card explicitly names Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite as its base and includes an exact-name comparison column. The comparison reports capability scores and prices, not total or active parameter counts.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Service use requires Google API and Gemini terms; terms prohibit extraction or replication of underlying model weights. Supports the proprietary API-access classification rather than an open-weight license.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite evaluation methodology — March 2026
sources.evidence: Explicitly identifies gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview as the Gemini API ID used for March evaluations. Does not establish that the later GA checkpoint is unchanged.

sources.title: Vertex AI release notes — March 3, 2026
sources.evidence: Historical March 3 entry calls the model public preview while writing the unsuffixed gemini-3.1-flash-lite ID. This conflicts with preview-versus-stable API naming, and does not explicitly bridge unchanged checkpoint identity to GA.

sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash Model Card — September 2, 2026
sources.evidence: Later first-party model card checked for retrospective disclosure; no Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite total or active parameter count appears.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Model Card — October 13, 2026
sources.evidence: Later first-party model card checked for retrospective disclosure; no Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite parameter-count comparison appears.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite — HTML model card
sources.evidence: Linked by the stable API documentation. HTML remains dated March 3, while its downloadable PDF is updated May 2026; both refer architecture to Gemini 3 Pro.

name.note: Use the official hyphenated display name.

developer.note: Google product, with model documentation published by Google DeepMind.

family.note: Catalog-normalized Flash-Lite subfamily within Gemini 3; the official later Flash-Lite card identifies this model as its base.

release_date.note: Exact stable release. March 3 was public preview; older Vertex notes use the unsuffixed ID for that preview. No inspected source explicitly states the preview and GA checkpoints are unchanged, so March is not transferred to this stable record.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is hosted API/product access under Google terms; no downloadable-weight distribution is provided.

license.note: Descriptive classification for hosted access under Google service terms; not an SPDX open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: No total count is disclosed in the inspected exact-model card, referenced architecture card, or later comparison cards. Exact-name searches across Google/DeepMind research and training/interpretability sources found no additional count disclosure; sibling counts are not transferred.

active_parameters_b.note: The architecture reference explains sparse activation but gives no numeric active count for this model. Later exact-name comparison and research searches did not supply one.

architecture.note: The stable documentation links this exact card; its architecture section explicitly delegates to Gemini 3 Pro, which specifies a sparse MoE Transformer. This is an explicit documentation chain, not a family-name inference. Expert counts and routing details remain unspecified.

context_window.note: Documented Gemini API input-token limit; Google Cloud also labels this the context window. The separate maximum output is 65,536 tokens. This is an endpoint specification, not a claim about training context or current callability.

modalities.note: Exact stable API page lists these supported data types. PDF is retained as the documented document input type; image/audio/video generation is not asserted.

reasoning.note: Thinking is explicitly supported; Cloud lists minimal, low, medium and high levels.

tool_call.note: Function calling is explicitly supported for the stable model.

description.value: Low-latency Gemini model for high-volume multimodal and agent workloads
description.note: The description is supported by the exact-model developer guide and needs no correction.

patch.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite
patch.notes: Stable release: May 7, 2026. March 3 was a preview; historical Vertex notes used the unsuffixed name, but unchanged preview-to-stable checkpoint identity is not established. Sparse MoE Transformer through the exact card’s architecture reference; total and active parameter counts are undisclosed.

summary: Confirmed the stable May 7, 2026 release, endpoint limits, modalities, reasoning and tool calling. Corrected official display-name punctuation, proprietary license classification and architecture to sparse MoE via an explicit exact-model documentation chain. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed after later-card and targeted research checks. Recorded the March preview naming conflict without inferring unchanged checkpoint identity.
